title: My experience with AI game dev and releasing my first Steam game
author: fiveohhwon
selftext:
Hi everyone, I just got through pressing release on my first steam game and I just wanted to give a post to my thoughts on my experience with AI game development and how I went through the whole process and hopefully it helps showcase my workflow and what I did to get here.

First of all, I’d like to say that I did not one shot this game. This took me months to build and iterate and test play and troubleshoot and test play some more. It was a very long process, but of course it was shorter because of the use of AI.

Now the technical bits: 

**Game Development**

I utilized Opus 5.5 for most of it, but the project did start out using Astra and I’ve also utilized Gemini 3.8 Flash along with 4 Argon. I used a mixture of Nano Banana 2 and GPT-IMAGE-2 for image generation, concept images, etc.

The game is built in Unreal with the use of Blender MCP and Meshy for the modeling.

I would try to take it one small feature or model or iteration at a time and play test frequently. One of the things that Astro was good at was spatial awareness. The rest aren’t as good so it took playing an iterating on things like towel physics or just how something should sound or just have something should feel

**Marketing**

I launched the game this morning with just around 400 wish lists and in order to get there it took a pretty big process and a lot of work.

I started by assembling a massive list of content creators, both small and medium. My list I think reached about 1700 instead of sending out just mass emails to all of them. I curated the list down to just about 300 that I thought would be interested in playing my game.

I reviewed some of their latest content and made sure that my hunch is correct and that they would you know be interested in playing my game and and I use these details to personalize each of the 300 emails that went out and I included a steam key as part of my outreach.

This got me about 50 responses mostly all positive and interested and then some looking to get additional keys so they could try out co-op. I spent a lot of time replying and talking to content creators and giving additional keys out. A lot of these content creators provided feedback and you know we were able to fix some early issues before the game was released and so I’m really thankful for them.

Similarly, I did the same research for curators for steam connect and built a list similarly so I could use all of my 100 curator connects available. This led to about 10 reviews and recommendations early on, and hopefully it still leads to more. I did have to manage the list frequently you know 10 people here there would decline and then I would have to go through and add 10 more and that happens a few times not 10, but you know one or two here and there.

I’ve also spent a lot of time watching these creators, YouTube videos and Twitch streams and engaging with them on their platforms and listening to feedback and trying to improve the game based on their feedback as well. it’s terrifying watching someone play your game on Twitch.

And then social media I posted on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram reels daily most got 1200 to 1400 views nothing blew up my hope was to make something go viral it didn’t happen I mean it still could of course and I’m going to keep posting and promoting, but these channels still did lead to some of my wish lists, but I think the outreach did more for those then my social media did.

So this morning, I woke up to 400 wishlists. My plan was to press the release button around 1:00 CST but I decided to hit the release button and of course I had my AI do it.

I hope at the very least the post was insightful or contained something helpful to the next person.
